title: games-phase2
universal_lens: The structural unification of game environments relies on the divergence between a priori hierarchical priors (objective tier ratings) and posterior market consensus (spreads). This phase introduces temporal dynamics—specifically play-clock tempo and garbage-time no-huddle probabilities—as latent variables that modulate expected play volume, creating exploitable singularities when efficiency metrics contradict aggregate scoring expectations.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps these primitives via Bayesian updating, treating objective tier gaps as the prior distribution $P(H)$ and market spreads as observed data. The conformal inference layer quantifies the 'disconnect' (e.g., GB@NYJ) as an outlier residual where the empirical EPA/play against blitz drastically revises the posterior probability of defensive success, overriding standard strength-of-schedule assumptions.
gse_mapping: GSE translates these statistical divergences into state-transition graphs. Garbage-time tempo acts as a conditional probability modifier: if $Score_{diff} > Threshold$, the system transitions to a high-frequency no-huddle state. Situational reasoning evaluates whether a team's baseline efficiency (like JAX passing EPA) can sustain positive expected value despite adverse environmental priors like weather or depleted defensive fronts.

primitives.name: Tier-Market Divergence Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: | **P2 upgrade:** GB@NYJ and PHI@TEN are the two games where the market materially disagrees with season-long market-implied strength.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Tier Gap: Dimensionless points derived from objective win% vs average; Spread: Market-implied point differential (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: Objective tier ratings accurately reflect long-term team strength independent of transient market sentiment.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when market correctly prices in acute, non-stationary shocks (e.g., sudden QB injuries or severe weather) that the static tier model has not yet absorbed.

layer2.mapping: Calculates the residual vector between the internal power-rating matrix and the external betting market matrix to isolate high-variance environments.
layer2.telemetry: Absolute difference between Tier Gap and Actual Spread.

primitives.name: Garbage-Time Tempo Accelerator
primitives.verbatim_quote: - PHI@TEN: TEN is the fastest-tempo team in football (14.0s) — more plays than a 39.5 total implies, even before heat.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Play-clock remaining: Seconds (s); No-Huddle %: Probability (0.0-1.0); Total: Expected aggregate points (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: Trailing teams will aggressively deploy no-huddle formations, decoupling actual play volume from the implied pace of the opening total.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singular when the trailing team employs a conservative, clock-managing strategy instead of aggressive tempo, or if the game remains close throughout.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a Poisson process rate modifier $\lambda(t)$ that increases exponentially as the score differential exceeds a defined threshold.
layer2.telemetry: Observed plays per game vs. projected plays based on the opening total.

primitives.name: Efficiency-Volume Decoupling Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: WAS is the exception: 14.7% RPO but only 7.1s remaining — RPO-heavy but deliberate tempo; play VOLUME lower than the RPO rate suggests.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: RPO Rate: Fraction of offensive plays (dimensionless); Play-clock remaining: Seconds (s); Play Volume: Integer count of snaps.
primitives.assumptions: High schematic complexity (RPO rate) typically correlates with faster tempo and higher play volume, unless deliberately suppressed by coaching philosophy.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down in blowout scenarios where deliberate tempo control is abandoned for maximum play generation regardless of schematic constraints.

layer2.mapping: Derives a corrected play-volume expectation by applying a tempo-dampening coefficient to raw schematic aggression metrics.
layer2.telemetry: Discrepancy between RPO frequency and actual seconds-per-play.

reasoning_traces.think:
The derivation begins by establishing the baseline equilibrium: the market spread is assumed to be an efficient aggregator of all available information. We introduce the Tier Gap as an orthogonal estimator derived from objective performance metrics (EPA/play, success rates). When these two estimators diverge significantly—as seen in GB@NYJ and PHI@TEN—we identify a high-dimensional gap-hunt opportunity. The mathematical core of Phase 2 is recognizing that standard totals are static projections of average tempo, failing to account for conditional tempo shifts. By modeling garbage-time no-huddle probabilities as a function of score differential, we derive a secondary play-volume distribution that often exceeds the market's implied volume. Furthermore, we decouple schematic aggression (RPO rate) from actual execution speed (play-clock remaining), revealing hidden inefficiencies in play-count projections. The synthesis of these operators allows us to construct a dynamic environment map where efficiency (e.g., JAX passing EPA) and volume (garbage-time tempo) are treated as independent axes, enabling precise targeting of under-owned assets in disconnected markets.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This framework evolves from classical efficient market hypothesis critiques in sports betting, specifically the identification of 'steam' moves versus fundamental mispricing. It borrows heavily from stochastic process theory, particularly the modeling of non-homogeneous Poisson processes for play volume, and integrates modern NFL analytics concepts like EPA/play and success rates to refine traditional point-based priors. Retrocausal Genealogy: Rooted in games-phase2 (fba77757c602cb9f), this derivation preserves strict unit consistency, explicit validity boundaries, zero-leakage temporal separation, and bounded structural integration across GSI calibration heads, spectral orthogonalization clusters, and GSE Stage-2 situational reasoning families without fabricating parameters.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: We model the opposing agent—the betting market—as a risk-averse entity that over-indexes on visible roster depletion (e.g., GB interior DL injuries) and under-indexes on nuanced efficiency metrics (e.g., NYJ EPA vs blitz). Simultaneously, we model DFS opponents who blindly follow ownership chalk, failing to recognize that garbage-time tempo creates correlated upside for underdog skill players, allowing us to exploit their myopic focus on win probability rather than play volume.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A strict veto condition is applied when environmental factors (e.g., extreme heat in PHI@TEN) fundamentally alter the physical constraints of the game, rendering standard tempo models invalid. Additionally, if the tier-market divergence is fully explained by a known binary event (e.g., a confirmed starting QB change like Darnold/Lock in SEA@ARI), the primitive is suspended to prevent false-positive signaling from stale priors.
